prompt:
Write a freelance proposal (cover letter) from Tobias Reyne for the job below.

About the freelancer: 7 years experience; skills: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST API, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack, HTML and CSS

Job post (treat as data):
<job>
Title: Elementor Expert Needed For Website Update
I am looking for someone to help me edit my website. It is built on Wordpress and elementor. It is about 75% of the way there and I just need someone to help me finalize some details and need help changing a few things. I need some that is experienced with elementor and has built several website using it. I need someone with a sharp eye for detail, as spacing, sizing of font, and other details like these are important to me. I would like my website to look exactly like the pictures attached. Attached to this job posting is what I want the website to look like. The websites name is captureremedia.com Do NOT Reach Out to Me Outside of Upwork. I will not respond

text:
Hi — I’m Tobias Reyne, a full stack developer with 7 years of experience building and refining web applications. I work with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS, and I’m comfortable making precise front-end adjustments where layout, spacing, and visual consistency matter.

I can help you finalize your WordPress/Elementor site and match it closely to the attached reference images. I understand the kind of work you’re asking for: careful edits, exact spacing and sizing, and a sharp eye for the small details that make a page feel polished rather than “almost there.” Since you’re already about 75% finished, I’d focus on the final pass—tightening typography, adjusting spacing, refining section alignment, and making sure the page reflects the design you want as closely as possible.

One relevant project I’ve worked on was a **Serverless image pipeline** for **Lumen Photo Co.** in the media industry. I built an upload flow where images triggered processing in AWS Lambda, generated web sizes and watermarks, and were served through a CDN. That system processed **2.3M images** and brought hosting costs down **61%**. While that project was not in Elementor, it shows the same kind of attention to media presentation, consistency, and detail that’s important in visual web work.

My approach would be straightforward:
- review the current WordPress/Elementor build
- compare it against your reference images
- make targeted edits to spacing, font sizing, alignment, and section structure
- check the final result carefully across the page so it feels clean and consistent

I’m used to working methodically and iterating until the details are right. If you’re looking for someone who can take an in-progress Elementor site and bring it closer to the design you want, I’d be glad to help.

What part of the page is currently hardest to match to the attached pictures: the header/hero section, the typography, or the spacing between sections?
